tei:titleStmt.tei:title: שְׁעֵה נֶאֱסַר
Sh'eh Ne'esar — a pizmon seliḥah for 17 Tammuz by Shlomo ibn Gabirol (ca. 1050)

tei:div.tei:head: Sh'eh Ne'esar — a pizmon seliḥah for 17 Tammuz by Shlomo ibn Gabirol (ca. 1050)

tei:lg.tei:l: Shoot a glance at the bound, who was delivered into the hand of Babel and Seir;
sighing to You for oh so long, pleading like a young child,
on the day the enemy prevailed and the city was breached.
Low bent, I thus slap my palms on the day my sorrow was fivefold —
for the calf’s foot the tablets left me,
so too the daily sacrifice was destroyed and I was imprisoned,
a godlet was placed in the utmost Palace and from Their counsel I was held back,
and the grain-offerings ceased, and Your law the foe burned in fire,
on the day the enemy prevailed and the city was breached.
Much I grieve and panic on the day Shaddai cast me out,
as the viper from the north swept me away like grain;
light darkened, as Sheshakh like a ball tossed me, and the hunter
sent out his hand, as did the antelope and the billy-goat,
on the day the enemy prevailed and the city was breached.
O my heart’s splendor, and my fortress, will Your rage forever smoke?
Do You not see the weary people who have been darkened like an oven?
Mend my breach with the Perezite and from the thorns pick the rose!
Build the glorious house to return the boundaries of the Carmel and Bashan!
Open Your eye and take vengenace on Ezer and Dishan!
Judge for the silenced, so that the destroyers and kindlers will be paid back
for the day the enemy prevailed and the city was breached.

tei:note.tei:p: Nebuchadnezzar. For “from the north” see Jeremiah 1:13-14.
Esau, i.e. Edom, i.e. Rome. See Genesis 25:27.
The Messiah, a descendant of Perez through the line of David.
Often used as a synecdoche for the land of Israel. See Isaiah 33:9, Jeremiah 50:19, and Nahum 1:4
Descendants of Seir (see Genesis 36:21, 30), thus representing Edom, i.e. Rome.
